To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
docosahexaeonenoic acid (DHA) and other polyunsaturates inhibit constitutively activated Akt (PKB), which in turn suppresses the proliferation of the human breast cancer cells MDA-MB453.

docosahexanoic acid (DHA), and other polyunsaturates (PUFA), inhibit constitutively activated Akt phosphorylation in a breast cancer cell line and this inhibition may contribute to their anti-cancer effect.
DHA, and to a lesser degree other PUFAs, suppressed the growth of human breast cancer cells by blocking Akt phosphorylation on two residues.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of DHA on breast cancer cells, in particular, the inhibition of constitutively active Akt, which is a common event in many cancers, and the modulation of fatty acid oxidation.
the effects of DHA on the Akt signaling pathway and fatty acid metabolism in a human breast carcinoma cell line.
the effects of DHA on deregulated phosphorylation, metabolism and proliferation of the breast cancer cell line.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DHA inhibits constitutively activated Akt in the breast cancer cell line and this effect is accompanied by a decrease in MUFAs and increase in β-oxidation.

DHA is an inhibitor of Akt phosphorylation on both T308 and S473 in MDA-MB453 cells and this effect is associated with the reduction in the amount of free MUFAs and SFAs and the elevation of 2,4-Dienoyl-Coenzyme A reductase expression.
DHA is a potent inhibitor of constitutively active Akt, which is a major contributor to cancer growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the inhibition of constitutive Akt activation in MDA-MB453 cells is achieved by a complex mechanism that involves the suppression of free and phospho-MUFAs, and the elevation of 2,4-Dienoyl-Co-A reductase, and that this mechanism is specifically and most efficiently activated by DHA.
DHA, and to a lesser extent other PUFAs, inhibit the growth of the MDA-MB 453 cells through their inhibition of Akt phosphorylation.
DHA, and possibly other omega-3 PUFAs, may be used to treat breast cancer with a high level free MUFAs and deregulated phosphorylation on T and S residues of Akt.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DHA can suppress the growth of breast cancer cells by blocking the phosphorylation of Akt on both T308 and S473 residues.
DHA is the only PUFA that is able to suppress Akt phosphorylation in MDA-MB453 cells.
dietary PUFAs may be used as a potential tool to suppress the growth of breast cancer cells with aberrantly activated Akt.
